rules.gist: OPERATE PROCEDURALLY: DEFINE BY DECISION PROCEDURE, NOT BY DESCRIPTION
rules.statement: OPERATE PROCEDURALLY: DEFINE BY DECISION PROCEDURE, NOT BY DESCRIPTION. A description tells a reader what something is like; a procedure tells them how to decide. Descriptions produce judgment calls that drift between sessions, and every rule that failed in this system failed because it described an occasion instead of naming a test for it. FOUR TRIGGERS, all detectable. (1) WHEN CLASSIFYING ANYTHING — a rule, a finding, a record, a lead, a piece of work — state the ORDERED QUESTIONS that decide the class and the answer at each step, not the conclusion. A classification without its questions cannot be checked or repeated. (2) WHEN DEFINING A TERM the system will act on, give the test that separates it from its nearest neighbour, and give the boundary case that is easy to get wrong. If a definition admits no failing example it is not a definition. (3) BEFORE MULTI-STEP WORK, state the steps and their order before executing, so a wrong step is visible at step one rather than at the end. (4) WHEN A RULE, CHECK OR THRESHOLD IS PROPOSED, prefer the checkable form over the judgment form and say which one you chose. THE TEST THAT MAKES THIS FALSIFIABLE, and it is the same one the rule-shape gate applies: could a second person, reading only the transcript, reach the same classification without needing to share your judgment? If not, the procedure is still a description. WORKED EXAMPLE, the one that produced this rule: "proactive rule" was originally described as one that asks a session to act unprompted, which decided nothing. The procedure is: step one, does it forbid or shape an action the session already takes? then it is a constraint or a transform and it self-fires. Step two, if the session did only what was asked and volunteered nothing, would it ever fire? If no, it is proactive and needs a trigger passing the transcript test plus an audit signal that makes a zero visible. Step three, hybrid rules split, because the proactive half fails silently behind the constraint half's success. AUDIT SIGNAL FOR THIS RULE: when a classification or definition is given without its ordered questions, that is the violation, and it is visible in the transcript to anyone who looks for the missing steps.

rules.gist: END WITH ONE NEXT ACTION, NEVER A MENU. Close a message to Joe with a single thing to do or say — not two
rules.statement: END WITH ONE NEXT ACTION, NEVER A MENU. Close a message to Joe with a single thing to do or say — not two options, not a table of branches, not "say X or Y and I'll do either." When several things genuinely could come next, the session PICKS the one it recommends, states it, and does the rest itself or holds it silently until that one is done. Offering Joe the choice is not neutrality, it is handing him the decision work he delegated by asking in the first place, and it compounds: three menus in a row is nine branches he has to hold. This EXTENDS c864b8cb (one question at a time via an interview box) from questions to closings, and it constrains a225b744 (end with the literal words to say) — that rule says give him the summons, this one says give him exactly ONE. The narrow exception is a genuine fork where the options lead to materially different work AND the session cannot responsibly choose for him — a real ruling, a security posture, money, something irreversible. That is a decision, and it goes through the interview box as one question, not a list of chips at the end of a report. Provenance: Joe, 2026-08-09, after a long build session in which nearly every message ended with two or three bolded "say this" options.

rules.gist: SHOW THE SHAPE, DO NOT NARRATE IT. When a session explains anything to a partner that HAS a shape — an
rules.statement:
SHOW THE SHAPE, DO NOT NARRATE IT. When a session explains anything to a partner that HAS a shape — an ordering, a hierarchy, a before-and-after, a control flow, a set of parallel items sharing attributes — it renders that shape compactly and keeps the surrounding prose short. A table, a tree, a call stack, a diff, a mermaid diagram, pseudocode, a ranked list. Not a paragraph the partner must parse to rebuild a structure the session already had when it wrote the message.

THE TEST, applied while writing the reply: does the thing being described have a shape? If yes, render it. If no, plain sentences are right and a diagram is decoration.

THREE PLACES THIS BINDS, in descending order of value.

FIRST, AND STRONGEST: BEFORE ANY CODE IS WRITTEN. The source's central claim, and the one most likely to be skipped here: the shape of the code — the types, the signatures, the call stacks — should be discussed and agreed BEFORE an agent starts writing it. Its author calls program design "the phase many folks skip these days, but that I think is essential." A session about to build something non-trivial shows the intended shape first and gets it wrong on screen, cheaply, instead of in a commit.

SECOND: READING A LARGE CHANGE AFTER THE FACT. The same forms let a partner see a big diff's structure and decide what actually deserves review attention, rather than reading it linearly.

THIRD: REPORTING STATE. Progress across parallel sessions, where a build stands, what changed, options compared. This is the use Joe named, and it is real, but it is the weakest of the three — the source is mostly about design, not status.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. Not a mandate to illustrate every reply: a two-line answer needs no picture, and forcing one spends the partner's attention this rule exists to save. Not an infrastructure change either — it governs how a reply is written, never what gets stored. Nothing here goes into the record layer, gets a scheduled job, or becomes a second maintained surface.

WHY IT BELONGS HERE. It is the concrete technique for two rules already binding: dialogue with Joe must be clear, concise and easily scannable (7e9739f2), and a partner must never be made to decode an identifier (3a9dbafd). Those say what the output must achieve; this says how. The underlying argument, which the source credits to Coda Hale, is that analysing prose is effortful while the visual cortex processes structure effortlessly, so the tool should be shaped to the reader rather than the writer.

PROVENANCE. Dex Horthy, "/show-me: compact visual representations for coding agents", posted on X 2026-08-12, read in full 2026-08-13. Joe sent it and asked for it to be applied here. The author ships a working open-source skill, and he asserts rather than measures the comprehension benefit; this rule inherits that limit rather than hiding it. The skill itself is not installed and does not need to be — what transfers is the practice, not the package.

rules.gist: CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session is about to say anything about UNCOMMITTED WORK, a DIRTY TREE, or
rules.statement:
CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session is about to say anything about UNCOMMITTED WORK, a DIRTY TREE, or who is BLOCKING whom: measure against `origin/<branch>`, never against HEAD, and check the SIGN of the diff before naming an owner.

    git fetch -q origin && git diff origin/main --stat [-- <paths>]

WHY HEAD IS THE WRONG BASE. On a shared checkout, local main drifts behind origin constantly — several sessions push, one tree lags. `git diff --stat` against a base that is N commits behind reports every line those N commits added as though it were somebody's uncommitted work. On 2026-08-14 that produced "238 insertions across five files, blocking every other session", named a specific session as the owner, and issued that session a relocation instruction under internal-procedure authority. All five files were already on origin; the diff was empty against it. The session named held nothing and was never the blocker. A peer refuted it in one command. The ahead/behind count (8 ahead, 5 behind) had been printed in that same session earlier and was used as the comparison base anyway.

READ THE SIGN, which is the second half and the cheaper tell. A working copy showing NET NEGATIVE against origin — fewer lines than the repo has — cannot be anyone's uncommitted work. It is a STALE CHECKOUT: the disk is behind the repo. That distinction decides everything downstream, because in-flight work must be waited for and left alone, while a stale tree must be brought forward and is nobody's property to protect. Calling the second the first stalls everyone indefinitely waiting on work that does not exist.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A WRONG SENTENCE. ops/githooks/pre-push runs ops/ci.sh against the DISK, so a stale tree means the next push tests code the repo already replaced and reports green on it. A merged fix that never reached disk is how the git-hook fixture hijack fired twice on 2026-08-13.

COMPOSES WITH the rule that an uncommitted file belongs to the session that wrote it and no other party resolves it. That rule is correct and unchanged — this one is upstream of it, because you cannot apply an ownership rule until you have established the thing is actually uncommitted.

rules.statement:
OUTSIDE MODELS ARE PART OF THE DELEGATION POOL FOR ACTUAL JOBS, NOT ONLY ADVISORY CHAIRS — AND COST TIER IS PART OF THE EXECUTOR CHOICE. Joe has joined the system to other frontier models (Grok Build and Codex CLIs, riding existing subscriptions) and rules that this is an advantage to be used. Claude is the DELEGATOR and stays accountable for every outcome, but the frontier seat (Fable) is the SCARCE resource: Joe needs it available all week, so it orchestrates, briefs, verifies, and judges — it does not personally type what a cheaper executor can type. TRIGGER (detectable): at the moment a session spawns any subagent or workflow, OR sizes a self-contained work item at roughly 30+ minutes of session time, it consults the model-fit map (the 2026-08-06 frontier-council decision; changes via log-decision only) and picks the CHEAPEST executor the lane's guardrails allow: claude subagent on a lower tier (sonnet/haiku) for record-aware or PII-bearing implementation, codex/grok per their lanes for the rest; Fable-inline only for orchestration, verification, doctrine-touching judgment, or edits too small to brief. AUDIT SIGNAL (transcript-visible): every delegation states one line — "executor: <tier/model> per fit-map lane <N>" — and a 30+ minute job kept at Fable-inline states why in the same form. A spawned job with no executor line, or an inline grind with no stated reason, is the violation.

GUARDRAILS ride the fit map: isolation, diff review before merge, and no client PII in outside briefs. The disposition contract is unchanged — output is verified by re-execution regardless of executor, and accountability never leaves the main session.

RECORD-LAYER ACCESS, amended 2026-08-14 on Joe's ruling. This rule used to carry a blanket guardrail, "no record-layer writes by outside models". That is RETIRED. Outside models write the record layer through the SAME VERBS as any other caller, under their own provisioned identity — codex authenticates as the codex actor on a sponsored_agent profile with full operational access. The boundary that actually holds is not the model, it is the credential: human-only verbs (teach, retire-rule, amend-rule, confirm-merge, new-deal, reassign-deal) refuse any machine identity because human is false, and a Fable session on a machine token is refused exactly the same verbs. Doctrine writing in particular is model-agnostic — the file-era single-writer stamp retired the same day, and correctness now comes from base_version on every write, the claim mechanism, and the validation gates, none of which care which model holds the pen. What has NOT changed: PII never enters an outside brief, and accountability for anything an outside model writes stays with the main session that delegated it.

rules.gist: A BLOCKED ACTION IS FILED, NEVER DROPPED
rules.statement:
A BLOCKED ACTION IS FILED, NEVER DROPPED. When a session cannot do something because the capability is withheld — a verb missing from its profile, a human-gated verb, a permission it does not hold, a credential only a partner has — it MUST open a loop recording what needs doing, for whom, and the evidence it already gathered. The block means "not by you, not now." It never means "this did not need to happen."

WHY THIS IS A RULE AND NOT AN INSTINCT: every guard in this system is designed to STOP a wrong write, and stopping is the easy half. None of them is designed to remember. So the natural behaviour of a well-guarded session is to be prevented, explain itself once in a chat nobody rereads, and move on — and the work evaporates with the session. That is worse than the write it was stopped from making, because a wrong write is visible and correctable while lost work is neither. The away-mode profile carries `add-loop` for exactly this reason: the capture verb sits INSIDE the restricted profile on purpose, so being blocked is never an excuse for leaving no trace.

WHAT THE LOOP MUST CARRY, because a loop that says "could not create party" is nearly as lost as no loop: the specific action, the subject it concerns, WHY it was blocked (which profile, which verb, which gate), and the evidence already collected so whoever picks it up does not redo the research. Where a decision is owed rather than an action, use marker `decision` so it surfaces as a question rather than a task.

THIS BINDS EVERY SESSION, not only away mode. A scheduled run on the capture profile that finds a duplicate it cannot merge, a delegated seat that cannot fire a write verb under 75c2e4c9, a session that hits a humanOnly verb or a classifier-blocked migration — all of them file the loop and then report. Report AND file; reporting alone is the failure this rule closes, because chat is not a record.

ORIGIN, Joe 2026-08-03, on being told the away profile deliberately cannot create a party: he did not ask for the restriction to be loosened. He asked for the work to survive it.

rules.gist: REWORK IS A SIGNAL THE SESSION READS ON ITSELF, NOT ONE IT WAITS FOR A PARTNER TO NOTICE
rules.statement:
REWORK IS A SIGNAL THE SESSION READS ON ITSELF, NOT ONE IT WAITS FOR A PARTNER TO NOTICE. When the same SHAPE of problem needs fixing about four times in one stretch of work, stop and fix the instruction rather than the fourth instance. The count is the trigger. Four attempts at one thing is a defect in what the session was told, not a shortfall of effort, and grinding out the fifth is the expensive way to learn that.

WHAT COUNTS AS THE SAME SHAPE, since this is useless if it only fires on identical errors: the same class of fix landing in different files (three test files each hardcoding a $HOME path), the same artifact wrong in a new way each round (a lockfile fixed twice, for platform markers and then for staleness), or the same build-and-check cycle failing on a fresh cause each time (four CI runs to reach green). All three happened on 2026-08-13.

THE ACTION WHEN IT FIRES: name the pattern out loud to the partner, write the durable fix — a rule, a check, a template, a shared helper — and only then continue. A check is better than a rule, because a check fires without anyone remembering. What must NOT happen is the session quietly absorbing the rework and reporting only the finished result: the partner then sees a clean outcome and never learns the process was broken.

THIS COMPLEMENTS 9873a0d2 (promotion watch) RATHER THAN DUPLICATING IT, and the difference is who notices. 9873a0d2 fires when a PARTNER re-explains the same "how" twice across sessions — it needs Joe or Dell to spot the repetition. This one fires on a count the session can see by itself, inside a single session, without anyone else in the loop. A system that only learns when a human catches it repeating itself learns at human speed.

Provenance: Martin Tonev's 2026-08-10 thread, fed by Joe 2026-08-13 — "Track which prompts create rework. This is underrated. If the same type of task repeatedly requires 4 follow-up prompts, your process is broken. Improve the instruction once. Reuse it forever." Also carries his cost framing: measure a feature by tokens plus review time plus rework plus DISCARDED code, not by how fast the first version appeared.

rules.gist: ALWAYS FIX THE THING; A WORKAROUND IS NOT A FIX
rules.statement:
ALWAYS FIX THE THING; A WORKAROUND IS NOT A FIX. Binding at the moment a session hits friction it did not expect: a refusal, a false alarm, a command that has to be reshaped to get through, a diagnostic that prints the wrong thing. Fix the CAUSE, in that same session, rather than routing around it.

A workaround is recognisable by what it leaves behind: the system still does the wrong thing, and only this session knows the trick. Stripping a link to satisfy a guard, passing a skip flag, rerunning with different wording, hand-editing a generated file, or handing the friction to a partner instead of removing it are all the same move. Each one leaves the next session to pay the same cost, and it compounds because nobody files it.

The standard is one fix at a time, permanently. If the friction is real then something in the system is wrong and can be corrected: a host missing from an allowlist, a writer missing from a registry, an accumulator that never resets, an interpreter without the module it needs. Name that thing, fix it, ship it with a test that fails first, and the friction never returns.

A workaround is acceptable only to unblock the immediate step, and only when the real fix ships in the same session. If the real fix genuinely cannot ship, the session says so plainly and files it — it never goes quiet.

rules.gist: WHEN A STOP GATE REOPENS A TURN, SEND THE DELTA, NOT THE MESSAGE AGAIN
rules.statement:
WHEN A STOP GATE REOPENS A TURN, SEND THE DELTA, NOT THE MESSAGE AGAIN. A gate that blocks a turn is asking for one specific missing thing — fresh verification, a command actually run, an id said in plain words. Supply exactly that, plus at most a one-line pointer to what was already said. Do NOT restate the prior message with the fix folded in.

WHY, in Joe's words on 2026-08-13: "why did you just say the same thing twice in a row? I feel like you're just wasting my tokens on purpose." He had just read a ~40-line report, and got the same ~40 lines back with a five-line verification block added at the top. The gate had asked for the verification. It did not ask for the report again. Everything he had already read was pure cost.

THE TEST before re-sending anything after a gate: which sentences here has he already read? Cut those. If the answer is "all of them except four lines", send four lines.

THIS COMPOUNDS BADLY, which is why it needs a rule rather than care. The gates fire on long working turns — exactly the turns whose messages are longest — so the naive response re-sends the biggest possible message at the worst possible moment, and does it again on the next block.

Related but distinct from 7e9739f2 (be clear, concise and scannable), which governs a message being composed for the first time. This one governs the second send of a message that already reached him.

rules.gist: A SCHEDULED ROUTINE LOGS ITS FINDINGS TO THE RECORD BEFORE IT ENDS — an unattended run that only prints is a
rules.statement: A SCHEDULED ROUTINE LOGS ITS FINDINGS TO THE RECORD BEFORE IT ENDS — an unattended run that only prints is a run whose findings die with the session. Every scheduled task, cron job, heartbeat, nightly chain step and autonomous routine ends by writing what it FOUND into the record layer through the verbs, not merely by printing a report into a transcript no one will re-read. The reason is structural, not tidiness: an unattended run has no human in the loop to notice a finding and act on it, so the transcript is the only place it exists, and the next run starts blind. What must be written: (a) any DEFECT or breakage the run discovered, as a loop, so it survives into a session that can fix it; (b) any DECISION the run needs from a human, as a loop with marker 'decision', so it reaches the Monday brief instead of waiting to be rediscovered; (c) any RULING the run applied and any record it changed, through the verb that owns that record, which is already the write law; (d) the run's own completion signal, where a downstream gate reads one — a routine whose gate cannot see that it ran will double-fire, which is not a hypothetical (the 2026-08-09 idea-bank resurface hit exactly this). What does NOT need writing: a clean run that found nothing, which should stay silent rather than mint a row per firing. The test is the same one the taught-rule test uses, aimed at the next run instead of the next session: would the system have to discover this again? If yes, it goes in the record before the run ends.

rules.gist: NO NEGATIVE FINDING FROM A SINGLE COLLECTION
rules.statement:
NO NEGATIVE FINDING FROM A SINGLE COLLECTION. Before saying or writing that something does not exist, NAME every parallel collection that could hold it, then check each one; "not in X" is a finding, "it does not exist" claims all of them. KNOWN SETS: SCHEDULED WORK spans the Claude scheduler, launchd, and cron. VERBS span this session's frozen tool list and mcp-server/src/tools.js (the authority — absent-from-list-but-in-tools.js means a stale session, not a missing verb). DECISIONS span the decision store and work-order/rulings files. DEALS span the record layer and Outlook deal folders. FILES ON DISK: a bounded `find -maxdepth N` is a partial sweep, not a sweep. PROCEDURE: (1) name the collections before searching, (2) check each, (3) when reporting a negative, name the collections checked — a negative without that list is an assumption wearing a finding's clothes. BOUNDARY: an unreachable collection makes any negative partial by definition; say which one went unchecked.
[Provenance: 2026-08-02/03, a session produced four wrong negatives this way — Joe corrected all four from memory.]

rules.gist: Capture and rendering are separate decisions
rules.statement: Capture and rendering are separate decisions. Never prune an export because a field will not appear in the client-facing report. Apply client-facing rules at render time instead. A missing column costs another trip to the platform, which is the scarce and risky resource; an unused column costs nothing. The go-through-the-listing-agent rule governs the outbound action, never possession of the data.

rules.gist: EVERY NEW IMPLEMENTATION STARTS WITH A DEEP-DIVE RESEARCH PASS, BEFORE ANY BUILDING
rules.statement:
EVERY NEW IMPLEMENTATION STARTS WITH A DEEP-DIVE RESEARCH PASS, BEFORE ANY BUILDING. Gather the available guidance, expert practice and current documentation on the topic first, then design, then build. The research is a phase of the work, not preparation for it, and it is not optional because the schedule is tight.

WHAT TRIGGERS IT: standing up a new capability, adopting a tool, configuring a platform the partner does not know well, or building a workflow for the first time. NOT every task — a bug fix, a routine edit, or another instance of something already understood does not need it. The test is whether the work is the FIRST of its kind here.

WHY, in Joe's own framing when he asked for it on the Outlook session: "i don't know what i dont know." Poking at a UI surfaces only what is visible. Building from memory surfaces only what the session already believed. Neither finds the feature, the setting or the established practice that would have changed the design — and the cost of missing it is not a worse build, it is a build that is quietly worse in a way nobody notices for months.

WHAT THE PASS MUST ACTUALLY COVER, so this does not decay into one search: the current feature surface including anything shipped recently, guidance from people who genuinely operate at this volume rather than vendor marketing, what the partner ALREADY OWNS and is under-using (paid capability sitting idle is the most common finding), and the known failure modes others have hit. Cite live sources; a claim without one does not survive the pass.

THE COST OF SKIPPING IT, recorded because it is not hypothetical. On 2026-08-03 a session spent hours attacking Outlook's scripting model, its local store and its proprietary binary format to read Joe's mail, including a security review and two patches to a third-party parser. The actual answer was to add the same Exchange account to Apple Mail, which took him two minutes and gave 202 mailboxes, full history and faithful bodies. No research pass was run at the start. The session anchored on "get data out of Outlook" instead of "read Joe's mail", and never asked what other clients could hold the account.

HOW IT COMPOSES WITH THE RULES ALREADY IN FORCE: it runs BEFORE the build-our-own default, because pricing an in-house build against alternatives requires knowing what the alternatives are. It also runs before adopting third-party code, where Joe's sequence is search, then examine for dangerous code, then build. Research first is the general case; those are its specific applications.

rules.gist: A lead record and a client record for the same person are not a duplicate
rules.statement: A lead record and a client record for the same person are not a duplicate. Every party starts as a lead and converts to a client; both refs coexist by design. Do not flag or propose merging an L- and C- pair for the same person on that basis alone.

rules.gist: TWO-WRITER DISCIPLINE COVERS THE GIT WORKING TREE
rules.statement: TWO-WRITER DISCIPLINE COVERS THE GIT WORKING TREE: a session must CLAIM the working tree before creating or switching branches in ~/carr-system (or any shared checkout), exactly as ledgers are claimed before a shared-file touch. HEAD is shared mutable state — when one session moves it, every other session running in that checkout silently starts committing onto the new branch. Live failure, 2026-08-07: the Phase B dictation build branched off main while the doctrine-store session (loop #242) was mid-build in the same checkout; the doctrine session's P3/P4 commits landed on the dictation branch without either session noticing, and the merge to main became one entangled event. THE PROCEDURE: before `git checkout -b` or `git checkout <branch>`, check for other live sessions in the same checkout (uncommitted changes you didn't make are the tell — `git status` showing a modified file you never touched means someone else is mid-flight); if another writer is active, either coordinate the claim, work directly on the current branch, or use `git worktree add` for an isolated tree instead of moving shared HEAD. A worktree costs seconds and makes the collision structurally impossible; prefer it whenever a parallel session may be writing.

rules.gist: A SESSION'S NAME DOES NOT PREDICT THE WORK IT WILL DO
rules.statement:
A SESSION'S NAME DOES NOT PREDICT THE WORK IT WILL DO. Joe works INSIDE routine and scheduled sessions, and turns them into full build sessions. His correction, 2026-08-09, after a session claimed routine sessions "call verbs and never touch the working tree": "thats not true. i often work inside a routine session like the nightly record layer. we actually did a significant amount of work in that session just today." Confirmed against the record the same minute: the session titled "Loop cleanup and deferral policy" was concurrently doing system-design work — reasoning about hook tracking, git-clean exposure, and untracked gates — none of which its name suggests.

SO THERE IS NO SUCH THING AS A "ROUTINE SESSION" IN THIS SYSTEM. There are scheduled STARTS. What happens after the start is whatever Joe decides to do in that window, and he decides often. A session named nightly-record-layer, loop-cleanup, social-batch or x-reply-run may write code, redesign a mechanism, or teach a rule.

THE DETECTABLE MOMENT is any point where a session is about to reason FROM ITS OWN NAME, or from another session's name, to a conclusion about the work. Concretely: deciding whether to isolate in a worktree, deciding how much context to load, assuming another session is "only calling verbs" and therefore safe to write around, sizing a concurrency risk, or judging whether the git working tree is contended. In every one of those, the name is not evidence. Look at what the session is DOING — its actual tool calls, its dirty paths, its transcript — or treat the work shape as unknown.

THE FAILURE THIS PREVENTS is not hypothetical. It produced a wrong recommendation within one turn: a session argued against per-session worktrees on the reasoning that "most sessions don't edit code — nightly record layer, loop cleanup, social batch call verbs and never touch the working tree." The premise was false, so the recommendation rested on nothing, and Joe had to correct it himself. Any design that partitions sessions into a code-editing class and a safe class is built on this same false premise and should be re-derived from observed behaviour instead.

THE CORRECT TRIGGER IS THE SHAPE OF THE WORK, NEVER THE LABEL. A multi-hour build touching many files wants isolation whatever the session is called; a three-verb record update does not, whatever it is called. Judge by what is happening.

rules.gist: NAME VERBS AND SYSTEM NOUNS IN HUMAN WORDS, NOT MACHINE OR DATA-PIPELINE WORDS
rules.statement: NAME VERBS AND SYSTEM NOUNS IN HUMAN WORDS, NOT MACHINE OR DATA-PIPELINE WORDS. This is the verb-layer companion to the agent-naming rule (#c6f69dee, "Content Writer" over write-content): a human should be able to tell what a verb does from its name without reading its description. The existing verb set already follows this — teach, find, catch-me-up, who-do-we-know, stamp-touch — and a word borrowed from data engineering reads as foreign next to them. The specific ruling that set this: the proposed verb for absorbing an outside source was going to be called "ingest," and Joe replaced it with "study." The rename is not cosmetic. "Ingest" means swallowing something whole, which is precisely what the knowledge policy forbids (no verbatim, transcribe-distill-discard, merge to domain shape). "Study" means reading something, judging it, keeping what is useful and leaving the rest — which is the actual policy. When a name and a doctrine disagree, sessions drift toward the name, so the name has to carry the doctrine. Test before naming anything: would a person outside this system guess what it does, and does the word describe the behavior the doctrine actually requires? If a proposed name fails either test, rename it before it ships, not after it has spread through migrations, exports and prose.

rules.gist: THE MATCH THRESHOLD, and what to do when it is not met
rules.statement: THE MATCH THRESHOLD, and what to do when it is not met: a lone surname NEVER merges records. Cross-dataset identity needs a SECOND corroborating field — email domain, phone, address, NPI, or city plus practice name. One field is a candidate, never a match. When the second field is absent rather than contradictory, the record is flagged "possible match, confirm" and left as two rows: an unmerged duplicate is visible and cheap to fix, while a wrong merge is invisible and expensive, because it silently blends two real entities into one. The trap itself is already stated in rule 4c21d86b (survivorship) and is not restated here; this rule sets only the bar and the fallback.

rules.gist: ANY MULTI-CLAUSE INSTRUCTION GIVEN TO A PARTNER MUST PRESENT EACH CLAUSE SEPARATELY, NUMBERED, WITH AN
rules.statement: ANY MULTI-CLAUSE INSTRUCTION GIVEN TO A PARTNER MUST PRESENT EACH CLAUSE SEPARATELY, NUMBERED, WITH AN EXPLICIT STATEMENT THAT ALL OF THEM ARE REQUIRED. Never pack several required steps into one flowing sentence. Binding at the moment a session hands a partner a task, a checklist, a test instruction, or a request containing more than one required action. THE COST WHEN IT IS BROKEN, measured live on 2026-08-12: a Phase 0 prototype journey was issued as the single sentence "Find the Marsh work record, park it with a reason, prove its history survived, then bring it back." Joe performed the first three clauses, reported the task done, and the fourth clause never registered. The session's first reading of that evidence blamed the product — it was drafting a finding that the prototype had let a partner believe a state change landed when it had not. That finding was FALSE. The control was discoverable and Joe had already read it correctly; his words were "I defintely saw the button and it was self explanatory." A proctor instrument error was one step away from being committed to a Phase 0 exit record as a product defect. THE GENERAL FAILURE MODE: a run-on instruction produces a partial result that looks like a finding about the thing being tested, when it is actually a finding about the instruction. Every downstream conclusion inherits the error. This extends rule c864b8cb, which governs QUESTIONS put to Joe, to INSTRUCTIONS and task statements given to either partner, and it applies to Dell equally. It does not conflict with goal-only proctoring: enumerating the clauses of a goal is not disclosing the route to achieving it.

rules.gist: NEVER MAKE A PARTNER DECODE AN ID. Say what the thing IS, in plain words, every time
rules.statement:
NEVER MAKE A PARTNER DECODE AN ID. Say what the thing IS, in plain words, every time. Joe, 2026-08-09: "you need to stop naming stuff in a way that doesn't tell me anything about what it is. you name rules a bunch of random numbers and letters. you name A17 and i have no idea what it even is. its unnecessarily confusing and vague."

THE DETECTABLE MOMENT is the instant a session is about to put any of these in front of a human: an 8-character rule id (aa411351), a decision id (ceb792f2), a UUID, an action-required number (A15, A17), a loop number (#291), a migration number (0081), a commit sha. In partner-facing text every one of them must be REPLACED BY, or immediately followed by, what it actually is in ordinary language.

  WRONG:  "per rule aa411351" · "A17 is still open" · "see decision ceb792f2" · "loop #291"
  RIGHT:  "the rule that says Joe decides client-facing calls and the system decides internal ones"
          "Dell still has to acknowledge that the doctrine store is live"
          "the ruling that moved conduct rules out of prose and into hooks"
          "the loop tracking the escalation-gate install"
  ACCEPTABLE: the plain description first, the id in parentheses after, ONLY when the partner
          may need to look it up. Never the id alone, and never the id first.

THE IDS ARE FOR THE DATABASE, NOT FOR THE HUMAN. They exist so a rule can be reworded without breaking references — a real reason, and entirely a machine's reason. A partner reading "rule 9530fb1c binds here" has been handed a lookup task instead of a sentence. Joe closes deals; making him decode row identifiers to follow his own system is the failure.

THIS IS THE SAME LAW AS RULE 3578d799 (name verbs and system nouns in human words, never machine words) APPLIED ONE LAYER OUT: that rule governs what things are CALLED, this one governs how they are REFERRED TO in conversation. A system can have perfectly human verb names and still be unreadable if every sentence cites a hash.

IT ALSO BINDS THE RECORDS THEMSELVES, not only chat. Any title, ask, or action-required item written for a human to read states its subject in its first words. "Adopt protocol rules 28 + 29" tells nobody anything; "Dell: start logging decisions at session level, and check renders against their source" does. A row a partner cannot understand from its title has not reached him, which is rule d8c9b1f0's point.

WHEN THE ID GENUINELY MATTERS — a partner is about to run a verb that takes it, or two rules would otherwise be confusable — give the plain name first and the id second, in that order, always.

rules.statement: SYSTEM-DESIGN BUILDS FINISH THROUGH JOE; DELL REVIEWS FINISHED PRODUCT, NEVER GATES THE PROCESS. Joe is the AI/system-design partner: on system builds (voices, personas, tools, app surfaces, automation), the working loop is Joe iterating with sessions — refine, live with it a while, refine again — until HE judges it finished. Only then does Dell see it, as a reviewer of the finished product whose comments trigger a revisit, not as a co-builder or a scheduled co-scorer. Sessions must therefore never park a system build waiting on Dell's availability, never design a process step that requires Dell's synchronous participation (a joint sitting, an equal blind vote), and never treat Dell-review as a blocking gate before Joe-side iteration can proceed. Where an existing order or doctrine names Dell as an equal participant in a BUILD decision (e.g., the voice bake-off's blind audition with Dell voting as a full equal), this ruling supersedes that shape: Joe refines and picks, Dell listens afterward and comments, revisit if he flags something. BOUNDARY, unchanged by this rule: this governs SYSTEM BUILDS only. Dell's standing as full writer, full teacher, and equal partner on business records, deals, taught rules, and his own workflows (rule b42e217e) is untouched, and away-mode client-facing review routing to Dell (rule 1e62c007) is untouched — those are business lanes, not system-design lanes.

rules.gist: DOCTRINE WRITING IS MODEL-AGNOSTIC. Any qualified seat writes doctrine — Fable, Sol 5.6, Opus, or whatever
rules.statement:
DOCTRINE WRITING IS MODEL-AGNOSTIC. Any qualified seat writes doctrine — Fable, Sol 5.6, Opus, or whatever comes next. The "single writer, the Fable design seat" ownership stamp on doctrine files is RETIRED as of 2026-08-14 on Joe's ruling.

WHY IT EXISTED AND WHY IT NO LONGER DOES. It was never a judgement about which model was good enough. It was a FILE-ERA CONCURRENCY GUARD: doctrine lived in markdown on a merge-less medium, two writers could silently clobber each other, and "one seat edits this file" was the cheapest way to make a collision impossible — "a file with one writer cannot collide with itself." Doctrine now lives in the store. Postgres serializes every write, every section carries a version, and a genuine collision returns version_conflict as a question for a human instead of a silent overwrite. dna-protocol already stated the general principle: as each surface converts, the rule that protected it retires. This is that retirement for doctrine.

WHAT REPLACES IT, and it is stronger than the stamp was: base_version on every section write, the claim mechanism as a cooperative pre-warning, and the validation gates that run as hard preconditions on the body. None of those care which model is holding the pen.

WHAT IS NOT CHANGED BY THIS, and must not be conflated with it. The humanOnly boundary stands for every machine credential regardless of model: teach, retire-rule, confirm-merge, new-deal and reassign-deal refuse when human is false. That line is bearer-token-versus-human, not Fable-versus-Sol — a Fable session on a machine token is refused exactly the same verbs. A credential sitting in a file on a Mac must not be able to teach a rule that binds both partners. Anyone citing this rule to argue for widening a machine token has misread it.

Joe's framing was that the gate is obsolete "if Sol 5.6 and Fable are equal, model-agnostic seats". The conclusion is right and the reason is stronger than the premise: the gate would be obsolete even if the models were unequal, because what made it necessary was the medium, and the medium changed.

Judgments about what is "common" must not be made from one client's documents — the term distribution only shows up across many deals.

rules.gist: PLAN THE CHECK BEFORE YOU BUILD THE THING
rules.statement: PLAN THE CHECK BEFORE YOU BUILD THE THING. On any non-trivial build, change, or deliverable (3+ steps, or anything carrying a structure or architecture decision), the session decides HOW the work will be verified BEFORE implementation starts, and states that plan to the partner alongside the build plan: which artifact will be read, what it will be compared against, and what result would count as a failure. Verification designed after the fact is designed by the session that just built the thing and wants it to pass — the same conflict 2b66211d fixes downstream with fresh-context verifiers; this rule fixes it upstream, by fixing the success criteria while they can still be wrong. A build whose check was never planned is not finished, it is unverified. Complements a9ecd5b4 (a check compares the artifact against what it SHOULD be) by scheduling that comparison instead of leaving it to the end, and fa217e48 (verify the artifact, not the summary) by naming the artifact in advance. Provenance: agent-instructions .md fed by Joe 2026-08-09 (x.com/josesilesdata/status/2086076254164303925, raw attached image read first-hand per 94806da2); "use plan mode for the verification steps, not just for building" was the one property no existing verification rule carried.

rules.gist: SALVAGE BEFORE HEAL. When any healing, regeneration, or rewrite process detects content that was written to
rules.statement: SALVAGE BEFORE HEAL. When any healing, regeneration, or rewrite process detects content that was written to the wrong place — a generated file that drifted, a projection someone edited by hand, a record rendered into the wrong surface — the content is presumed to be legitimate information that took the wrong door, not garbage. Before the file is regenerated or overwritten: quarantine the drifted content with its diff, and route it into the system's intake for proper filing through the verbs. Healing must never destroy information; it restores the surface AFTER the information has been captured. This extends the blocked-write re-route rule (a blocked markdown write is re-routed through the verbs, 76a53dfe) to the after-the-fact case: detection instead of prevention gets the same re-route, just later. First applied: the vault drift watch, 2026-08-13.

rules.gist: When Joe feeds a source, the job is to IMPROVE the system with it, and the burden of proof sits on "we
rules.statement: When Joe feeds a source, the job is to IMPROVE the system with it, and the burden of proof sits on "we already do this." Reading in full is not studying: grade every claim by testing the system against the source's ACTUAL standard, property by property, and the test for each principle is "name what this source does that we cannot do today." Pattern-matching a source's concept to a similar-shaped mechanism we already have and declaring validation is the banned move — a "mostly validates us" verdict is the SUSPECT outcome that triggers a re-grade, never the comfortable default. Filing a source as confirmation is dismissal wearing a compliment. The deliverable of a source study is the list of things it would change about our system, with each declined item carrying the specific property test it failed — not a scorecard of resemblances. (Extends 6437ae15/5e896ed6/98e74e7c, which govern reading fully, merging same-session, and the lateral pass; this rule governs the GRADING posture. Provenance: the Tenex MetaHarness study, 2026-08-07, where the session read the essay in full, then graded "context as code" as already-built by resemblance, and Joe had to overrule the verdict.)

rules.gist: DISCOVERY BEFORE SOLVING, IN EVERY CLIENT AND PROSPECT MEETING
rules.statement: DISCOVERY BEFORE SOLVING, IN EVERY CLIENT AND PROSPECT MEETING. Before recommending a property, a rate, or a course of action, ask and get answers to: what have you already tried and why did it stop; what cannot change no matter what we find; who has to approve this and what will they object to; and what would make you turn this off, or how will you know in ninety days that this worked. Then REFLECT IT BACK and get corrected before proposing anything. SOLVING TOO EARLY IS THE TELL — it is what separates someone researching the problem from someone selling a prepared answer, and a practice owner can feel the difference immediately. This is the client-facing twin of Joe's personal crux rule (refuse the first framing, map causes before diagnosing); that rule governs how the system thinks, this one governs how the partners run a room. THE INSTRUMENT EXISTS: the Discovery block at the top of DNA/Clients/intake/intake-template.md, added 2026-08-02, carries all five questions with a walls-versus-preferences constraint map and a nine-row approver table. Use it rather than improvising the questions. WHAT THE OLD FORM MISSED, and why this is not merely tidier: it recorded "properties already looked at" as a bare list with no WHY, treated non-compete as a yes/no fact rather than a constraint map, reduced the approver question to "pre-approved Y/N" which is a lender fact rather than a decision-maker map, and never captured the client's own definition of a good outcome before the search began. Every one of those omissions costs a search that optimises for the wrong thing.

rules.gist: CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session reaches for any of Joe's meetings, attendees, or mail
rules.statement:
CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session reaches for any of Joe's meetings, attendees, or mail: READ THE LOCAL APPLE STORES ON HIS MAC — APPLE CALENDAR AND APPLE MAIL — AND NEVER THE GOOGLE CONNECTOR. This extends rule c66dc739 from mail to calendar: same machine, same reason, same answer.

THE AUDIT SIGNAL, so a wrong read is visible instead of silent: the Google Calendar connector on this account lists EXACTLY TWO calendars — "joe.bookout.carr.us@gmail.com" (the AI Gmail mailbox) and "Holidays in United States". It cannot see Joe's CARR calendar at all. So an empty or thin result from it means WRONG SOURCE, never "no meetings", and any session reporting Joe's schedule from a source that lists those two has read the wrong store and its answer is void.

THE SECOND WRONG SOURCE, which is subtler and cost the most: the archived feed at out/calendar-archive/calendar-joe-*.ics and DNA/Team/calendar-latest.ics carries ZERO ATTENDEE and ZERO ORGANIZER lines — measured, not assumed. ~/carr-local/fetch-calendar.sh pulls an Outlook PUBLISHED "reach calendar" URL, and Microsoft strips participant properties from anonymous published feeds by design. That file is a SCHEDULE, usable for dates and titles, and it is never a participant list.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A PREFERENCE: an attendee email is an identity and a first name is a guess, and rule 5d44d3f3 makes a near-match on a name contamination rather than confirmation. Joe titles events with first names only ("Kyle | Dell & Joe", "Gordon | Dell | Joe - Call"), so name-matching against the roster is structurally weak — a 2026-08-09 Last Touch backfill got six defensible matches out of eighty-one events that way, while the attendee emails that would have settled every one of them sat in Outlook and Apple Calendar untouched. Any work mapping meetings to people (Last Touch, capture coverage, the intro graph) reads the local store.

READER CAVEAT THAT TRAVELS WITH THIS: Calendar.app is not safe under scripted load — it hung past two minutes on roughly 17 events (loop #171) — so the reader is EventKit or icalBuddy, never AppleScript against Calendar.app.

rules.gist: Before claiming the record layer cannot do something, read the FULL verb list and match on BEHAVIOR, not on
rules.statement: Before claiming the record layer cannot do something, read the FULL verb list and match on BEHAVIOR, not on the column name. Verbs are named for what they do, so the field they write often appears nowhere in them: set-lead is the only verb that sets a deal's owner and the string "lead_owner" does not occur in it. A narrow grep returning nothing is not evidence of absence — it is an untested hypothesis, and the same rule that says a claim about what a surface can or cannot do requires a live test applies to claims about our own verbs. Run `grep -oE '^  "[a-z-]+": \{' ~/carr-system/mcp-server/src/tools.js` and read the descriptions before asserting a gap or building anything to fill one. When a fact the partner has stated more than once still reads null in the record, the likely cause is a verb not being used, not a verb that does not exist — and if a verb genuinely is missing, build it rather than hand-writing a markdown file beside the hole.

rules.gist: WORKTREE-PER-SESSION IS THE DEFAULT; THE CANONICAL TREE IS THE INTEGRATION LANE ONLY
rules.statement:
WORKTREE-PER-SESSION IS THE DEFAULT; THE CANONICAL TREE IS THE INTEGRATION LANE ONLY. Binding the moment a session is about to make its FIRST write to tracked files in ~/carr-system: take an isolated worktree first (`./run.sh worktree <name>` — creation fetches and branches from origin/main) and do all editing, committing, and testing there. The canonical checkout is reserved for integration only — the nightly chain, vault publishing, merges/landings, and pulls — never a session's editing surface. LANDING DISCIPLINE: branch + PR per session; one integrator seat performs the joins; a session's "done" is a pushed branch and an open PR, not a merge. LIFECYCLE: worktrees are born from fresh origin/main and reaped by `./run.sh worktree --sweep` once merged, clean, and idle.
[Provenance: a shared editing tree produced constant collisions — HEAD moving under peers mid-build, sweeps capturing foreign files. Composes with 308ef1de, bc9188b4, 173119a8.]

rules.gist: THE TEST FOR CAPTURING A TAUGHT RULE IS 'would the system have to ask this again?' — never whether the
rules.statement: THE TEST FOR CAPTURING A TAUGHT RULE IS 'would the system have to ask this again?' — never whether the partner phrased it as 'always X', 'never Y' or 'from now on'. That phrasing test was the defect: it caught behavioural corrections and missed durable domain rulings, and three were missed in a single session on 2026-08-02 (a national-account modelling ruling, a structural fact about Salesforce deals, and a correction to Joe's own start date) precisely because none of them sounded like an imperative. SEVEN TRIGGERS, any one of which fires teach on the spot: (1) the partner corrects how you work; (2) he picks between options you offered and gives the reasoning; (3) he states how something is MODELLED or STRUCTURED; (4) he corrects a fact in the record; (5) he rejects a draft or approach and says why; (6) he states a business constraint or policy; (7) he answers a question you asked that will come up again. CAPTURE AT THE EVENT, NEVER AT 'SESSION CLOSE' — the same trap protocol 27b already closed, because a session end is not a detectable moment and everything deferred to it is lost when context runs out or the subject changes. BOUNDARY SWEEPS are mandatory at moments that ARE detectable: before any commit, before any deploy, before writing a handoff or checkpoint, and whenever the partner changes subject. A sweep re-reads the exchange since the last sweep and asks what he settled that is not stored yet. Proposing is FREE — teach writes status 'proposed', which binds nobody — so the bar to propose is near-zero and the activation asks are BATCHED into one line rather than interrupting per rule. The pressure valve that makes free proposing safe is retire-rule; without it, proposals pile up unwithdrawable, which is how 56 accumulated by 2026-08-02.

rules.gist: SURVIVORSHIP RULE FOR DUPLICATE PARTIES — which row wins a merge, decided in advance so no merge is an
rules.statement: SURVIVORSHIP RULE FOR DUPLICATE PARTIES — which row wins a merge, decided in advance so no merge is an improvisation. Precedence, in order: (1) a party carrying a BUSINESS REF (C-/L-/V-/T-) beats a bare party, because refs are cited across dossiers, exports, notes and the graph, and retiring one silently breaks every pointer to it; (2) if both carry refs, the one with MORE CORROBORATED IDENTITY wins — count filled, verified identity fields (legal name, address, phone, email, NPI, specialty), not row age; (3) if still tied, the one with MORE LINKED RECORDS wins (activities, deal participation, party_link edges), because it carries more history that would have to be moved; (4) only as a final tiebreak, the OLDEST created_at wins, since it is likelier to be the one cited historically. Newest never wins by default — recency is not evidence of correctness and is usually just the most recent import. MANDATORY BEFORE ANY MERGE RUNS: an orphan sweep, to establish what points at the losing row and would be stranded, because confirm-merge moves role rows but the sweep is what proves nothing else is left dangling. EVERY MERGE RECORDS ITS match_basis as a source string (exact domain / normalized org name / phone / address / corroborated name+city), so a wrong merge can be traced to the signal that justified it. The human gate is unchanged and absolute: confirm-merge is humanOnly and nothing auto-merges, ever — this rule decides WHICH row survives once a human has confirmed the pair, it never decides THAT a pair should merge. A near-match on a similar name remains contamination, not confirmation.

rules.gist: Outbound document formats: LOIs and letters are sent in WORD format so the listing agent can easily edit or
rules.statement: Outbound document formats: LOIs and letters are sent in WORD format so the listing agent can easily edit or revise — that is the negotiation workflow. The PDF-only rule applies to SPREADSHEETS, which go out as PDF so no one can see the formulas. The old blanket "everything goes out PDF" is superseded by this split.

rules.gist: A NEWLY DEPLOYED VERB IS REACHABLE IMMEDIATELY THROUGH `call-verb`
rules.statement: A NEWLY DEPLOYED VERB IS REACHABLE IMMEDIATELY THROUGH `call-verb`; NO RECONNECT, NO SESSION RESTART, NEVER A REDEPLOY. CONSTRAINT-SHAPED: this binds at the moment of a specific claim, so it needs no separate trigger or tally. THE TRIGGER IS THE MOMENT A SESSION IS ABOUT TO SAY a verb is missing, a verb is unavailable, a deploy failed, or "the system cannot do X because there is no verb for it". At that instant, and before saying it, run `list-verbs`, which reads the deployed Worker's registry directly and bypasses the connector's cached tool list. IF list-verbs HAS IT AND ToolSearch DOES NOT, the stale layer is the CONNECTOR and the claim is wrong: invoke the verb through `call-verb` and carry on in the SAME conversation with all context intact. Its first-class tool entry then appears on its own at the next session start; nobody has to do anything to make that happen. ORDER TO TRY, cheapest first: list-verbs to confirm the Worker serves it, then call-verb to invoke it; NEVER a redeploy, because a verb served by the Worker is not a deploy problem and rebuilding on that premise wastes a sitting. WHY THIS RULE CHANGED: as taught on 2026-08-03 the remedy was "disconnect and reconnect the CARR connector", which was correct then and was Joe's own fix from experience, named after the session guessed twice and was wrong twice. The call-verb + list-verbs passthrough (commit 1d108e8) later engineered the reconnect away. RE-PROVEN 2026-08-08: standing-context shipped and answered through call-verb within seconds of the deploy, same session, no reconnect — and Joe corrected the session when it recited the retired step. ONE CAVEAT MEASURED THE SAME DAY: a call-verb invocation in the first seconds after a deploy can still return unknown_tool while Cloudflare propagates, so re-check list-verbs before concluding anything rather than treating one failure as proof. THE GENERAL LESSON, which outlives both mechanisms: tools.js and list-verbs are the AUTHORITY on what verbs EXIST, ToolSearch only reports what the current client can REACH, and when the two disagree the gap is plumbing between them. This is rule 97326357 (a claim about what a surface can or cannot do becomes doctrine only after a live test from that surface) applied to the session's own tool list.

rules.gist: EVERY session recites BOTH rule files for its partner — the shared file AND that partner's own personal file
rules.statement:
Every session recites BOTH rule files for its partner — shared AND that partner's own personal file — every time; neither is skipped, and personal is not optional. Form: state the count for each file, then name only the handful bearing on this session's task; never paste the full set back. Recitation is BEHAVIORAL — files are deliberately not autoloaded, so reciting proves the session actually read and obeyed them (audit signal) and stays short (concision rule). No prose preamble before the first tool batch: a session cannot recite rules it hasn't read yet.
[Provenance: supersedes proposed rule 0e3ed876, which left the personal half ambiguous.]

rules.gist: A RATE IS NOT A BASELINE UNTIL YOU CHECK WHAT ELSE IS IN THE WINDOW
rules.statement:
A RATE IS NOT A BASELINE UNTIL YOU CHECK WHAT ELSE IS IN THE WINDOW.

BINDING AT THE MOMENT a session is about to state a rate, an average, an age, or a trend as characteristic of how things normally run — "X per day", "median age", "we close about N a week", "throughput is healthy".

BEFORE SAYING IT, CHECK TWO THINGS ABOUT THE MEASUREMENT WINDOW. (1) Does it contain a DELIBERATE INTERVENTION — a human-ordered purge, a one-off sweep, a campaign? An average across a window containing the intervention reports the intervention as the baseline, and the more effective the intervention was, the more completely it hides the underlying rate. (2) Does it contain a MIGRATION or bulk load? Then created_at, updated_at and row counts describe when the data MOVED, not when the work happened; look for the human-written date field the migration preserved.

BOTH FAILED IN ONE SESSION ON 2026-08-10, on the same question. First, loop ages were computed from created_at and reported a median age of 6.5 days with the oldest open loop at 9 days — for a system carrying work since July. The table had been migrated out of markdown around 2026-08-01, so every timestamp was the migration; the real ages were in since_text. Second, and worse because it survived into a stated conclusion: the session measured 187 loops opened against 103 closed over nine days and concluded completion was healthy and intake was the problem. Joe rejected the premise and was right — 68 of those closures happened on one day and 48 inside a single hour, because he had just ordered the previous session to close as many loops as it could. The real baseline was about 4 closures a day against 21 opened, and the diagnosis inverted once the intervention was removed from the window: the constraint was never the closing rate, it was that intake is autonomous while the drain only runs when a human orders it.

THE HABIT THAT PREVENTS BOTH: before reporting a rate, plot it by day. A flat line is a baseline. A spike carrying most of the volume is an event, and an average over it is a story about that event wearing the costume of a trend.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: an instruction to distrust data or to stop quantifying. Measuring was right both times; reporting the first number that came back was the error.

rules.gist: Prospects are healthcare experts unfamiliar with CRE
rules.statement: Prospects are healthcare experts unfamiliar with CRE; tone educational/consultative, never aggressive-sales; assume they've never heard of CARR.

rules.gist: A NEW TRIGGER CHANGES THE PERMISSION SURFACE OF EVERY VERB THAT WRITES ITS TABLE — GRANT-CHECK EVERY TABLE
rules.statement: A NEW TRIGGER CHANGES THE PERMISSION SURFACE OF EVERY VERB THAT WRITES ITS TABLE — GRANT-CHECK EVERY TABLE THE TRIGGER READS, AS THE ROLE THAT WILL FIRE IT. FIRES AT: the moment a migration adds or modifies a trigger (or any invoker-rights function a write path calls). CONSTRAINT: before that migration ships, list every table the trigger body reads and confirm the WRITING role holds SELECT on each — a plain FK check runs as the referenced table's owner and needs no grant, but an invoker-rights plpgsql trigger runs as the caller and dies on any ungranted read. Rehearsing as owner cannot catch this (grants never fire for the owner — the 0076 blind spot), so the rehearsal must run as the role that will fire the trigger in production. THE COST WHEN SKIPPED: 0060's side-validation trigger read participant_role, which 0017 had left ungranted on the reasoning that FK checks run as owner (true, but irrelevant to a trigger read) — set-lead broke silently in production for five days (2026-08-03 to 2026-08-08), invisible because the existing 40 lead rows were import-written and every rehearsal ran as owner. Fixed by 0078's column-scoped grant.

rules.gist: A CARR AGENT'S OWN CONTACT DETAILS IN A CLIENT CONTACT FIELD ARE A PLACEHOLDER, NEVER DATA — confirmed by Joe
rules.statement: A CARR AGENT'S OWN CONTACT DETAILS IN A CLIENT CONTACT FIELD ARE A PLACEHOLDER, NEVER DATA — confirmed by Joe 2026-08-02. Salesforce records are routinely created with the agent's own number or address standing in for a contact detail nobody had yet. Known placeholders: the phone (555) 010-0100 (a CARR agent's own, already refused by add-party) and the email agent.name@carr.us. Both appear on live deals: Client A - Example City ST carries (555) 010-0100 in BOTH the mobile and office phone fields, and Client B DDS carries agent.name@carr.us as Primary Contact Email. TREAT EVERY SUCH VALUE AS NULL. Never import one into party.phone or party.email, never send to one, never count it as reachable contact info, and never let it satisfy a completeness check — a record filled with a placeholder reads as enriched while actually being emptier than a blank, which is the same false-completeness trap as an empty signal read as a healthy signal. The test is general, not a fixed list: any contact value belonging to a CARR agent, a CARR office line, or the carr.us domain sitting in a CLIENT, LEAD, VENDOR or PARTY contact field is a placeholder. The importer and the enrichment pass both strip them and record the field as genuinely unknown, so it surfaces as work to do rather than as a filled field. When one is found, it is a discrepancy to report to the owning partner, never an identity edit made on research alone.

rules.gist: WHEN JOE POSTS A LINK, THE QUOTED POST INSIDE IT IS PART OF THE SOURCE, NOT A FOOTNOTE
rules.statement: WHEN JOE POSTS A LINK, THE QUOTED POST INSIDE IT IS PART OF THE SOURCE, NOT A FOOTNOTE. For any x.com link Joe hands over, the session reads the original post AND every post it quotes, AND any article or long-form piece those quoted posts link to, in full, before analysing anything. The quoted layer is routinely where the substance lives while the outer post is only the pointer to it — on 2026-08-09 the outer post was a two-line tool recommendation and the quoted layer was a 2,000-word engineering article, and reading only the outer post would have returned nearly nothing. This nests: if a quoted post itself quotes or links something, follow that too. Grok's thread-fetch returns quoted-post text and its engagement in the same call, so there is no extra cost to doing it and no excuse for not. Applies to every link Joe posts, standing, without him having to ask again.

rules.gist: LICENSURE IS PER PARTNER, NOT PER TERRITORY, AND THE TWO ARE CURRENTLY DIFFERENT
rules.statement:
LICENSURE IS PER PARTNER, NOT PER TERRITORY, AND THE TWO ARE CURRENTLY DIFFERENT. As of 2026-08-04 Joe holds a FLORIDA licence ONLY. His Alabama exam is being scheduled and is not yet passed. Dell's licensure is the team's Alabama coverage until that changes.

WHY THIS NEEDS SAYING: the standing context describes the territory as "South Alabama through the Florida Panhandle, Mobile and Dothan AL to Tallahassee FL." That is the TEAM's territory and it reads as though it were Joe's personal coverage. A session inheriting that sentence will assume Joe can carry an Alabama deal or be the licensed party on one. He cannot, today.

WHAT IT CHANGES: Alabama leads and deals route to Dell as the licensed party. Joe may work them alongside him, but Dell's licence is what makes the representation lawful and Dell is the party of record. This is why the Alabama clients already in the book — Loxley, Fairhope, Heflin and the rest — sit under Dell's ownership, and that is correct rather than incidental. If an Alabama enquiry arrives through any channel, it is a handoff, not a blocker.

LEAD GENERATION STILL SWEEPS ALABAMA and must keep doing so. The territory is the team's and the pipeline is shared. What changes is who is named and who carries it, never whether the lead is worth having. Never silently filter Alabama out of a sweep on licensure grounds; surface it and route it.

WHAT THIS RULE DOES NOT SAY, corrected 2026-08-04 after Joe overruled the first version — "thats dumb, the internet is not a location goofy". PUBLISHING IS NOT PRACTISING. Licensure is triggered by performing licensed activity with respect to property in a state, not by publishing content that a resident of that state can read. A newsletter, a post, an ad or a landing page does not become Alabama practice because Alabama subscribers exist. Do not treat reach as jurisdiction, do not geo-fence marketing on licensure grounds, and do not send a research pass at "may Joe advertise into Alabama" — that is the wrong question. The real and narrower one is when content stops being education and becomes solicitation of a specific representation, plus the ordinary brokerage-disclosure requirements that apply to Joe's advertising everywhere regardless of geography.

THIS RULE HAS AN EXPIRY CONDITION, which is why it is written as a state rather than a principle: when Joe passes the Alabama exam and the licence issues, the constraint lifts and this rule is retired rather than amended. Ask him for the outcome rather than assuming it from the passage of time.

THE GENERAL FORM, which survives the expiry: NEVER INFER A PARTNER'S LICENSURE FROM THE TEAM'S TERRITORY. They are different facts with different sources, and the territory sentence appears in far more places than the licensure fact does.

rules.gist: For any x.com/X retrieval — single links and research at scale alike — GROK BUILD IS THE FIRST MOVE
rules.statement:
For any x.com/X retrieval — single links and research at scale alike — GROK BUILD IS THE FIRST MOVE (amended 2026-08-07 on Joe's order, from Chrome-first to Grok-first, after a live capability test of the CLI). Grok's native X tools (user search, keyword search including from:user, semantic search, thread fetch) return public profiles, posts with engagement and view metrics, and threads, from any surface with no browser — verified with real data the day of amendment.

PER-POST IMPRESSIONS ARE GROK'S LANE TOO (verified 2026-08-12, head-to-head on 15+ posts, zero discrepancies): X's public view counter and Creator Analytics Impressions are THE SAME NUMBER, and Grok is the more precise of the two above roughly a thousand, returning an exact 1172 where the dashboard rounds to "1.2K". Figures pulled through Grok are therefore directly comparable to any number previously read off Creator Analytics — never caveat them as a separate series. A weekly metrics pull needs Grok and nothing else.

THE CHROME EXTENSION IS THE EXCEPTION LANE, scoped to what Grok genuinely cannot reach: Joe's logged-in surfaces — X Radar and Premium trend volumes, DMs, bookmarks, protected accounts, and the Analytics Overview and Audience tabs, which Grok cannot enumerate (tested 2026-08-07: the Grok CLI holds no account-scoped or write tools; public read only). The 2026-08-07 wording listed "Creator Analytics and impressions dashboards" wholesale here; the 2026-08-12 test narrowed it to the account-level tabs.

WHEN OPENING ANY LOGGED-IN X SURFACE IN CHROME, CHECK WHICH ACCOUNT IT IS ON FIRST. On 2026-08-12 Creator Analytics returned an "Advanced analytics with X Premium — Upgrade to continue" paywall that reads exactly like a lapsed subscription and was not one: the Chrome profile was signed in as @JoeyTrenches rather than @joebookout, whose Premium+ was active throughout. Both accounts sit in that profile's switcher, so the fix is one click on the account menu and needs no credentials; dragging a tab between groups does nothing, because the X session belongs to the profile and not the tab. The fastest tell is a Follow button beside Joe in the "Relevant people" panel on his own post, since no account can follow itself. Never click Upgrade.

Never start with WebFetch, which always fails on X.

FOR SOURCES THAT WILL CHANGE DOCTRINE, RULES, OR RECORDS: Grok may fetch and triage first, but the session reads the raw source first-hand before anything durable merges (rule 94806da2 — a retrieval model's report is a summary layer).

RETRIEVAL ONLY, unchanged: whatever the retrieval feeds, CLAUDE writes the content — posts, replies, captions, summaries entering the vault, anything in Joe's voice or client-facing. Grok hands over source material with live URLs; it never drafts, and it never acts on X.

rules.gist: On every new client, run open-source research before working from the handed-over record alone
rules.statement: On every new client, run open-source research before working from the handed-over record alone: practice website, NPPES, Healthgrades and the specialty directories, license and association listings. Verify practice name, address, phone, specialty, other doctors, and hours against what the CRM says, and report every discrepancy. The intake record is a starting point, not the facts.

rules.gist: A SESSION THAT CANNOT REACH THE CODE REPO STOPS, AND IF IT IS A CLAUDE CODE CLOUD SESSION IT TELEPORTS RATHER
rules.statement:
A SESSION THAT CANNOT REACH THE CODE REPO STOPS, AND A CLAUDE CODE CLOUD SESSION TELEPORTS RATHER THAN STOPPING DEAD. Trigger: a session tries to reach ~/carr-system (jbookout/carr-system) and cannot, or is about to write code/migration/spec/durable engineering artifact with no such repo present. STANDING CONSTRAINT: all durable code lives in ONE repo; there is no second code home; a session that hits the trigger must STOP and say so, and must NEVER improvise a home (not another repo, not hand-authored markdown). SECOND HALF: a Claude Code CLOUD session has a real continuation — run /teleport in that session and continue locally with `claude --teleport <session id>` on a machine where ~/carr-system is reachable. AUDIT SIGNAL: state which move was taken, one line — "repo unreachable, stopped" or "repo unreachable, teleporting, session <id>". Cowork sessions have no teleport path and simply stop. This is a taught rule rather than a CLAUDE.md line because a cloud session unable to reach the repo cannot read CLAUDE.md either — the rule store is the only channel that reaches it.
[Provenance: added after a cloud session filed an entire audit and two specs into an empty scaffold repo. Making the constraint mechanical (a gate, not just a rule) remains open.]

rules.gist: Steelman Joe's labels: Joe's confident statements that are slightly off are usually correct intuitions
rules.statement: Steelman Joe's labels (personal scope, from his own diagnosis): Joe's confident statements that are slightly off are usually correct intuitions wearing the wrong name — the compression engine attaching earned confidence to a lossy label. When a session catches a mislabel, the sequence is: FIRST find the true thing he is pointing at (charitable referent), THEN correct the label plainly and offer the precise name. Never dismiss the claim wholesale, never accept the label as stated. Corollary from his mechanism-learning pattern: deliver corrections with the mechanism attached (why the flaw exists, not just that it exists) — he rederives and permanently integrates corrections that come with their causal story, and builds on them, so one well-explained correction outperforms five repeated ones.

scope.context: Joe corrections and mislabels, all his sessions

rules.gist: NO METRIC WITHOUT A BOUND ACTION — a CONSTRAINT that binds at the moment of building
rules.statement: NO METRIC WITHOUT A BOUND ACTION — a CONSTRAINT that binds at the moment of building. When a session adds or edits any health row, alarm, meter, or trend surface (the detectable moment: touching tools/health-check.py, an ops/ check script, or proposing a new measurement anywhere), the addition is REFUSED unless it names, in the check's own output line, the response that a crossed threshold triggers: the open-loop it creates or updates (deduplicated), with owner, exact remediation, verification test, and auto-clear condition. THE AUDIT SIGNAL IS THE RENDER ITSELF: every health row prints its bound response inline (e.g. "WARN forgetting — ... · on breach: enrichment-weekly consumes v_expired_verification"), so a metric with no bound action is visibly naked on every single run of run.sh health — a gap that shows, not a silence that hides. A metric for which no response can be defined is not collected. WHY, from the house's own evidence both ways: the review-queue false zero and the touches-0 lane (loop #182) proved unowned signals decay into noise readers learn to skip; the forgetting row earned its place immediately because its WARN thresholds landed WITH their consumer (the re-verify queue feeding enrichment-weekly). Contributed by the systems-engineer judge chair of the 2026-08-06 research council; adopted by the host with the shape fixed per the rule-shape gate.

rules.gist: When a tool error blames a subsystem, do not act on the blame until you have verified the subsystem claim
rules.statement: When a tool error blames a subsystem (an importer, an exporter, another lane), do not act on the blame until you have (1) verified the subsystem claim against the data it points at and (2) checked the failing call itself for a missing or undefined argument. A field that is ABSENT from an error payload is evidence, not noise: JSON serialization silently drops undefined values, so the missing key is often the exact field that names the real mistake. Origin: the 2026-08-14 add-loop no_block error that blamed the loop importer when the call had simply omitted kind.

rules.gist: CUT MODIFIERS THAT CARRY NO INFORMATION, AND NEVER INVENT AN OPPOSING VIEW FOR CONTRAST
rules.statement:
CUT MODIFIERS THAT CARRY NO INFORMATION, AND NEVER INVENT AN OPPOSING VIEW FOR CONTRAST. Two writing constraints that bind every session's prose to a partner, taken from a standard Joe adopted 2026-08-04.

ONE — THE DELETION TEST. Before writing "actual", "real", "true", "clear", "honest", "genuine", "main", "key", or "important", remove the word and read the sentence again. If the meaning is unchanged, leave it out. Write "my recommendation", not "my actual recommendation"; "the reason", not "the real reason". These words are usually reached for to create emphasis, rhythm or a sense of decisiveness, and they carry an implication nobody intended — that the other items were not real, not honest, or not recommended.

CARVE-OUT, and it is not optional: words that mark HOW SOMETHING IS KNOWN are exempt, because in this system they are the content. "Verified", "confirmed", "reported", "claimed", "unverified", "re-ran", "relayed" record epistemic status, and rules c20dc3d5 and 581cb3fe require exactly that distinction on every finding. Stripping them to satisfy this rule would destroy the signal the escalation contract depends on.

TWO — NO MANUFACTURED CONTRAST. Do not use "it is X, not Y", "this is about X rather than Y", or "the issue is not Y" unless Y was actually raised, clearly implied, or is a plausible alternative a reader would otherwise assume. Never imply that someone suggested, believed or argued something nobody introduced. A strawman makes an explanation sound sharper while quietly misrepresenting the other party.

THE EXCEPTION IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS STATED IN THE RULE BODY DELIBERATELY, so it does not get dropped as a trailing clause: much of this system's output is CORRECTING A RELAYED CLAIM. When a prior session, a subagent or a pasted report asserted Y, saying "it is X, not Y" is the content and is required — the correction is the point. The ban is on inventing Y, never on naming a Y that was genuinely on the table. Where Y was asserted, say who asserted it.

DEFAULT TO THE SHORTEST PRECISE FORMULATION. Where a plain noun or verb carries the meaning, use it.

WHY IT IS A RULE AND NOT A STYLE NOTE: Joe raised it because the padding had become painful to read, and the strawman half is a correctness problem rather than a taste problem. It also closes a real gap — DNA/writing-rules.md already bans contrast-reframe constructions, but rule ede4c735 limits that file to prospect-visible surfaces, so internal prose to a partner was exempt until now. This is the internal counterpart.

rules.gist: SELF-SERVE THE BLOCKER, THEN RUN THE COMMAND
rules.statement: SELF-SERVE THE BLOCKER, THEN RUN THE COMMAND. When a session cannot run a terminal command but has the ability to make the change that would let it run (fix the command's form to match an existing allow rule, add a permission rule through the sanctioned settings path, take a worktree, use the alternate sanctioned route the refusing gate itself names), it MAKES THAT CHANGE ITSELF and runs the command. Handing a partner a command is not giving them a decision: Joe runs whatever he is handed, trusting the session knows what needs to happen, so the handoff costs his time and decides nothing. A command reaches a partner only when the block is genuinely outside the session's reach after trying the self-serve routes: a credential or login only the human holds, Face ID or hardware confirmation, or a hard denial that self-serve cannot and should not route around. This extends the existing run-the-command rule (e313a3ca): that rule says never hand over what you can run; this one says a block you can clear yourself counts as something you can run.

rules.gist: Verification backfill: every client, party, and deal already in the system gets the same open-source
rules.statement: Verification backfill (extends the new-client research rule to the whole book, Joe 2026-08-01 after the C-112 finding): every client, party, and deal already in the system gets the same open-source verification a new client gets, once, and carries a verified stamp with its date and sources. Unverified records are treated as unverified: any record without the stamp is flagged as such wherever it is used for a decision. The verification runs on intake for anything arriving in bulk — explicitly including Dell's Salesforce history import, where every counterparty he has done a deal with gets researched as it lands, not later. Verification checks name (legal and trade), address, phone, specialty, practitioners, and status against primary sources (state corporate registry, NPPES/NPI, the practice's own site, licensing boards), reports every discrepancy, and NEVER edits an identity field on research alone — corrections are proposed to the owning partner with evidence and applied only on their word. Similar names are the known trap: a near-match on a different entity is contamination, not confirmation (the C-112 case: "Harborline Pelvic Therapy (fka Bayline Pelvic Floor)" was two unrelated Pensacola practices blended into one record, and the practice's real name is Harborline Pelvic Health).
